dataset: VIIRS/NPP Black Marble daily gap-filled BRDF-adjusted nighttime lights VNP46A2
economic_mechanism: Cloud-screened nighttime radiance anomalies over fixed tourism-dependent resort footprints may proxy nighttime occupancy and activity while avoiding property-level collection
predicted_direction: Positive for activity radiance; disruption-dependent negative shocks
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; geographic mix; quarterly revenue
why_underused: 500 m daily global processing, quality layers and authenticated granule archive are technically demanding and unlikely to be standard in sell-side models
plausible_abnb_materiality: High if a preregistered basket covers many globally material leisure markets
unit_of_observation: Daily 500 m sinusoidal-grid tile/pixel with corrected radiance and quality flags
granularity: 500 m pixel and fixed destination polygon
publication_schedule_and_lag: Daily product; exact production latency and collection-specific reprocessing schedule need granule-metadata verification
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: 2012-01-01 observation history; public product availability evidenced by NASA archive materials
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Collection versions may be reprocessed; quality layers and granule production timestamps are essential
true_vintage_support: Potentially yes through collection version and granule production metadata; not yet verified from authenticated listing
access_method: LAADS archive/API after Earthdata Login; CMR metadata discovery
collection_restrictions: No access before approved credential sync; token only in ignored .env; never log URLs/headers containing it
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Clouds; moonlight; snow; fires; power outages; infrastructure changes; stray light; 500 m mixed pixels; collection reprocessing
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Using a later reprocessed collection or post-cutoff granule version; fitting cloud/gap-fill thresholds on full sample
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: History spans 23/23 events, but 0/23 strict eligible until credentialed granule production/vintage audit
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One metadata query and one granule header after credential approval
primary_feature_formula_if_selected: Median quality-screened radiance YoY change across fixed resort polygons minus matched resident-control polygons over the last 28 eligible days.
sensitivity_if_selected: Fraction of valid pixels with positive YoY radiance change under identical masks.
biggest_failure_reason: Radiance may be dominated by stable infrastructure and environmental artifacts rather than lodging occupancy
analyst_notes: Raw ex-ante score 80/100, but operational rank 2 because access is pending sync and the occupancy mechanism is experimental

dataset: NOAA Hazard Mapping System daily fire and smoke analysis
provider: NOAA NESDIS Office of Satellite and Product Operations
economic_mechanism: Smoke polygons and active-fire detections over destination and access-corridor footprints measure realized environmental disruption capable of suppressing trips, closures and outdoor amenity value
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; geographic mix; quarterly revenue; guidance downside risk
why_underused: Manual analyst smoke classification plus high-frequency geospatial archives are operationally awkward and usually used for air-quality rather than travel forecasting
geographic_coverage: North America including Hawaii and Caribbean
plausible_abnb_materiality: High for U.S./Canada destination basket but episodic rather than continuous
unit_of_observation: Daily smoke polygon with start/end, density and satellite; fire point with FRP
granularity: Polygon or point intersected with fixed destination polygons
publication_schedule_and_lag: Fire detections typically online by 08:00 ET and updated continuously; first smoke classification 11:00-12:00 ET, second 19:00-20:00 ET
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: 2005 archive start; daily availability schedule documented by NOAA
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Forward-processing system does not backfill gaps; 2022 system/format regime change; annual bundles were regenerated in 2025 and therefore are not literal historical vintages
true_vintage_support: Partial: dated daily operational files existed
access_method: Official KML/shapefile archive and product page; current regenerated annual bundles are not historical snapshots.
license_or_reuse: NOAA-produced data generally public domain/CC0 with attribution and no implied endorsement
collection_restrictions: No automated request until path-specific robots status is verified; cache daily files and metadata; no tactical safety inference.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Cloud cover; analyst subjectivity; satellite additions/removals; missing data not backfilled; 2022 classification/format change; regenerated archive timestamps.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Treating regenerated annual bundles as original vintages or assigning end-of-day smoke information to an earlier cutoff.
leakage_mitigation: Use dated single-day operational files only; exclude annual regenerated-bundle timestamps; preserve a 2022 regime break.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Observation history spans 23/23 events, but 0/23 are strict-eligible until daily-file availability and vintage handling are locked.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One product metadata page and one single-day archive file; gate denied, so zero requests.
biggest_failure_reason: Smoke is sparse, highly seasonal, and may proxy widely known wildfire news rather than incremental destination demand.
analyst_notes: Conditional only after permission and daily-file provenance audit; never use regenerated annual-bundle timestamps as historical availability.

dataset: Washington State Ferries traffic statistics rider-segment reports
economic_mechanism: Ferry riders—especially Anacortes/San Juan, Bainbridge, Vashon and other leisure-sensitive route segments—measure realized movement into island/coastal destinations; foot/vehicle mix and service completion help separate demand from capacity disruption
predicted_direction: Positive for rider growth; negative for cancellations or lost sailings
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; geographic mix; quarterly revenue; next-quarter guidance
why_underused: Ticket-booth operational counts split by route and fare/rider segment are less standardized than airport totals and require route-level commuter controls
geographic_coverage: Washington Puget Sound and Salish Sea; nine routes and twenty ports
plausible_abnb_materiality: Material to a regional leisure market, not consolidated ABNB alone; best as one node in a multi-market destination-ingress mesh
unit_of_observation: Quarter-route rider totals with vehicles, vehicle passengers, foot passengers and fare categories
frequency: Quarterly dated reports; dashboard has daily/by-sailing detail
publication_schedule_and_lag: Quarter-end reports appear generated about five to ten days after period end; examples: 2020Q4 report 2021-01-05 08:33:30, 2023Q1 report 2023-04-05 16:00:02, 2025Q2 report 2025-07-05 16:00:02
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: 2021-01-05T08:33:30-08:00 for verified sample in modeled cohort
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Dated PDF snapshots appear static; dashboard may be overwritten; later corrections policy not located
true_vintage_support: Yes for dated PDF report artifacts; no conclusion yet for dashboard
access_method: Official WSDOT landing page and linked PDFs; dashboard for discovery only
license_or_reuse: Public government reports; WSDOT open-data/reuse language requires source attribution and planning-use caveats; exact automation permission unresolved
collection_restrictions: No automated request until exact terms and path-specific robots rules allow it; cache exact PDFs; do not scrape reservations
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Route/service changes; canceled sailings; fare collection direction; commuter mix; suspended Sidney service; altered fleet capacity; route coding changes
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Using dashboard restatements or treating printed report generation time as web publication without corroboration
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Estimated 23/23 target events have a preceding completed-quarter report by cadence; exact per-report availability must be audited before eligibility
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One report landing page plus one dated quarterly PDF, but gate denied so zero requests
primary_feature_formula_if_selected: Latest dated report strictly before cutoff: YoY change in fixed leisure-route foot passengers minus YoY change in fixed Seattle/Bainbridge and Seattle/Bremerton commuter-control foot passengers.
sensitivity_if_selected: Use total riders instead of foot passengers with the same fixed route sets.
biggest_failure_reason: Single-region materiality may be too small and route counts may mostly reflect commuter/service-supply dynamics
analyst_notes: Operational rank 1 despite raw score tie because dated report artifacts offer the cleanest current PIT path; no ABNB outcome inspected

dataset: Short-Term Rental Registration annual reports and dated registration datasets
provider: NYC Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement
economic_mechanism: Registrations granted less refusals/revocations measure legally executable host supply under Local Law 18.
predicted_direction: More active registrations/net approvals should raise legal supply and potential nights; more revocations/refusals should lower it.
potential_abnb_target: nights booked; revenue; geographic mix; next-quarter guidance
why_underused: Registration determinations and processing friction are hard to normalize and arrive outside standard hotel/airline datasets.
geographic_coverage: New York City; annual council-district aggregates and registration-level snapshots
plausible_abnb_materiality: NYC is a major global destination, though Local Law 18 sharply changed the addressable STR market.
granularity: registration record and fiscal-year council district
history: FY23 onward; registration regime opened March 2023; dated snapshot verified Jan. 7 2026
publication_schedule_and_lag: Annual report due around Sep. 1 for year ended June 30; dated snapshot publication schedule appears irregular.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Annual append-only reports; downloaded registration files are dated snapshots.
access_method: Official report PDFs and dated downloadable datasets; aggregate before retention.
license_or_reuse: Public government records; exact automation licence not established
collection_restrictions: No direct request until terms and robots affirm intended paths; do not retain address/unit/listing URL or host information; retain borough/council-district aggregates only.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Major policy regime break in Sep. 2023; short history; status definitions and renewal wave change in Oct. 2026.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Current status snapshots can overwrite historical states; treating 2026 file as 2023 supply would leak.
leakage_mitigation: Use only a dated snapshot/report actually published before cutoff; never infer pre-regime observations; keep annual and snapshot series separate.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Approximately 11 of 23 guidance events have post-regime context; high-frequency snapshots only verified in 2026.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After permission resolution: one annual report plus one dated snapshot; retain only aggregate counts and release metadata.
primary_feature_formula_if_selected: Percent change in unique active registration numbers between consecutive dated OSE snapshots released strictly before the cutoff, aggregated citywide and never retaining addresses or listing identifiers.
sensitivity_if_selected: Use the grant-to-application ratio from the latest dated annual registration report strictly before the cutoff.
biggest_failure_reason: The regime is too new and NYC's legal home-share segment may be too small to explain consolidated ABNB.

economic_mechanism: Tax remittances capture realized paid transient-lodging receipts in Orlando before many conventional annual statistics.
predicted_direction: Higher year-on-year TDT receipts imply stronger realized destination lodging demand and potentially higher ABNB revenue/nights.
potential_abnb_target: quarterly revenue; nights booked; U.S. leisure demand; guidance direction
why_underused: Release-specific county tax receipts are scattered across dated PDFs and require vintage-safe parsing; often omitted from national tourism models.
plausible_abnb_materiality: Orlando is a very large leisure destination with meaningful STR and theme-park demand, but one county cannot represent consolidated ABNB.
unit_of_observation: USD TDT collections per collection month
history: Official indexed PDFs verified from at least Apr. 2019 through Oct. 2025/2026 reporting cycle
publication_schedule_and_lag: Typically roughly 1-2 months after collection month; many PDFs include exact FOR RELEASE ON time.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Separate release PDFs; some later reports contain historical comparisons but the original files remain available.
access_method: Official monthly PDF archive/quick links and fiscal-year XLSX remittance files.
license_or_reuse: Public official reports; exact site licence/automation terms not located
collection_restrictions: No automated request until exact terms and robots allow; cache original PDFs; redistribution terms unresolved.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Tax rate/budget changes; late or amended remittances; platform tax-collection policy; hotel-heavy mix; hurricanes/theme-park closures; collection-month versus booking-month lag.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Using a later cumulative table or current workbook could silently include revisions; using collection month before release leaks.
leakage_mitigation: Use the original report release timestamp, not file metadata; latest release must be strictly before cutoff; prefer monthly actual, not cumulative restatement.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Likely 23/23 events have at least one prior monthly release; exact event-level audit remains required.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After permission resolution: quick-links index plus one monthly PDF with explicit release timestamp; cache and checksum both.
primary_feature_formula_if_selected: YoY percent change in the trailing three-month sum of Orange County TDT collections from PDFs released strictly before the cutoff.
sensitivity_if_selected: Use the latest single released collection month YoY instead of the trailing three-month sum.
biggest_failure_reason: TDT is a lagging all-lodging/price signal dominated by hotels and theme parks rather than an early Airbnb-specific signal.

dataset: Business licences filtered to Short-term Rental Operator
provider: City of Vancouver Open Data Portal
economic_mechanism: Licence issuance, expiry and non-renewal measure legal active host supply and regulatory attrition.
predicted_direction: Faster net issuance or renewal survival should increase legal supply/nights; expiry attrition should reduce them.
potential_abnb_target: active host supply; nights booked; geographic mix; revenue
why_underused: Annual folder years, licence revisions and local-area detail are operational records that require careful event reconstruction and privacy aggregation.
plausible_abnb_materiality: Major international urban destination, but one Canadian city is a limited share of ABNB.
history: Folder years visible at least 2024-2025; full API may contain additional years but was not requested.
publication_schedule_and_lag: Current extract refreshed periodically; exact lag from licence system to portal unverified.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Current extract contains historical event dates and licence revision numbers but extractdate is 2026.
access_method: OpenDataSoft Explore API filter on businesstype; no-key.
collection_restrictions: Terms permit Open Data use; exact robots allowance for API path is unresolved; collect only licence type/status/dates/local area and exclude names/addresses.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Annual licence-type taxonomy changes; business-type consolidation; revisions; current extract survivorship; non-renewal may reflect data cleanup.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: A 2026 extract can revise or omit licences that existed at historical cutoffs.
leakage_mitigation: Require archived extracts or provider confirmation that issue/expiry events are append-only; otherwise prospective snapshots only.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: 0/23 verified from current extract; event dates span the cohort in principle.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After robots resolution: one API call limit=2 filtered to Short-term Rental Operator, excluding personal/address fields.
biggest_failure_reason: Historical status survivorship cannot be ruled out from the present extract.

dataset: NPS Visitor Use Statistics monthly visitation and overnight stays
provider: National Park Service Social Science Program
economic_mechanism: Monthly recreation visits, visitor hours and overnight-stay categories across tourism-dependent parks directly measure realized leisure presence and park lodging/camping pressure
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; geographic mix; quarterly revenue
why_underused: Park counting procedures vary and require a fixed park basket plus procedure-change controls; this complexity and noncommercial portal reduce standard investor use
geographic_coverage: More than 400 U.S. national parks; monthly standardized series from 1979
plausible_abnb_materiality: Potentially broad U.S. leisure coverage but only park-adjacent demand
unit_of_observation: Park-month recreation visits, recreation visitor hours and multiple overnight-stay categories
publication_schedule_and_lag: Preliminary monthly data generally available by the 15th of following month; parks can edit until calendar year is finalized in Q1 of following year
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: Monthly series available from 1979; API/service public by at least 2010 Data.gov catalog
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Preliminary values revised until annual finalization; final annual tables locked afterward
true_vintage_support: No public API vintage endpoint identified; current API likely returns latest/finalized values
access_method: NPS IRMA REST Stats service and custom query portal
license_or_reuse: U.S. federal public data; attribution and DOI/citation where supplied
collection_restrictions: No automated request until path-specific robots status is verified; use aggregate park data only
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Counter equipment failures; estimated data; procedure changes; closures; vehicle-to-person factors; park redesignations; double visits
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Backfilling a preliminary historical month with its later finalized value; ignoring counting-procedure changes
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: History spans 23/23 events; 0/23 recent-month observations strict eligible without archived preliminary vintages; finalized prior-year values may be eligible with conservative Q1-finalization evidence
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One API help response and one park-month row
biggest_failure_reason: Lack of preliminary vintages means the most decision-relevant recent months cannot yet meet strict cutoff rules
analyst_notes: Strong mechanism, but current-history API alone is insufficient for historical guidance replay

dataset: Annual Reports of Short-Term Rental Enforcement
provider: NYC Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement
economic_mechanism: Complaints, inspections, summonses and violations measure regulatory friction and forced supply withdrawal.
predicted_direction: Higher enforcement intensity should reduce illegal active supply and potential nights, conditional on reporting and policy changes.
potential_abnb_target: nights booked; revenue; active supply; geographic mix
why_underused: Municipal enforcement intensity is policy-specific, annual, and rarely standardized in travel-demand models.
plausible_abnb_materiality: "NYC is globally important but its post-2023 legal market is unusually constrained."
history: Official page lists annual enforcement reports 2016-2024; FY26 release announced separately.
publication_schedule_and_lag: Annual; exact publication date varies and must be verified per report.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Separate annual report PDFs retained by the agency.
license_or_reuse: Official page states materials are available for public and research use; automation terms unresolved
collection_restrictions: No direct automated request until terms and robots resolve; aggregate only; no respondent or address data.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Enforcement priorities, complaint channels, staffing and Local Law 18 create structural breaks; annual frequency.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Later reports may restate earlier totals; report-year values are not available until publication.
leakage_mitigation: Use the first published annual report strictly before cutoff; preserve report version; do not backdate report-year totals.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: All 23 events have some previously published annual enforcement context in principle; exact release calendar audit required.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After permission resolution: report index plus one annual report PDF; cache and checksum.
biggest_failure_reason: Annual policy-driven counts may measure enforcement effort rather than economically material supply removal.

dataset: Raw Monthly Ridership no adjustments or estimates
provider: Federal Transit Administration National Transit Database
economic_mechanism: Unlinked passenger trips on fixed airport-rail, ferry, inclined-plane and tourism-sensitive transit modes can proxy realized urban arrivals while system bus/heavy-rail totals act as local commuter controls
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; domestic geographic mix; quarterly revenue
why_underused: The NTD is familiar, but constructing fixed tourism-mode residuals across agencies and separating service supply from trips is uncommon in sell-side lodging models
plausible_abnb_materiality: High U.S. city coverage but no station-level segmentation
unit_of_observation: Agency-mode-month unlinked passenger trips, vehicle revenue miles/hours and vehicles operated in maximum service
history: Monthly time series back to 2002; current modal time-series file from 2014-present
publication_schedule_and_lag: Published on fixed monthly cycle around the 4th-7th with a two-month lag; reporters submit by end of following month
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: At least 2002 for monthly ridership history
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Raw file has no estimates/adjustments but reporters can correct submissions; complete file includes estimates and historical adjustments; current file overwritten monthly
true_vintage_support: No dated public release-vintage archive identified
access_method: FTA downloadable Excel/CSV products and DOT data portal
collection_restrictions: No automated request until path-specific robots status is verified; prefer raw file; cache each monthly release prospectively
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Agency/mode reporting changes; service cuts; late reporters; unlinked-trip double counting; pandemic regime; no station detail
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Using current corrected raw file as if it were the historical release; using estimated complete file without vintage proof
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: History spans 23/23 events, but 0/23 strict eligible until dated historical raw releases are located; prospective collector can establish vintages
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: Landing page and header of one raw release file
biggest_failure_reason: Two-month lag and no station detail may leave little incremental information after broader mobility/transport data
analyst_notes: Best treated as a broad control unless historical releases are recovered

provider: City of New Orleans Department of Safety and Permits
economic_mechanism: Applications, approvals, expirations and denials map the legal STR supply pipeline.
predicted_direction: Rising net issuance and renewal survival should increase active supply/nights; denials and expirations should reduce them.
potential_abnb_target: active supply; nights booked; revenue; U.S. geographic mix
why_underused: Application workflow events are city operational exhaust and require de-duplication of reapplications and conservative availability rules.
plausible_abnb_materiality: A material event/leisure market, but small relative to consolidated ABNB and highly seasonal.
publication_schedule_and_lag: Current portal refreshed frequently; exact event-to-publication lag unverified.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Application/issue/expiration dates plus overwritten current status; no changelog archive.
access_method: Socrata SODA API view en36-xvxg and CSV export.
license_or_reuse: Portal marks public access; exact dataset licence/automation terms unresolved
collection_restrictions: No direct request until terms and robots allow; exclude owner/operator/contact/address fields; aggregate by quarter and permit type.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Duplicate/re-filed applications, policy changes in 2023, corrected permit types, overwritten status, missing expiry/issue dates.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Current statuses and disappeared rows can create survivorship; event dates do not prove public availability on those dates.
leakage_mitigation: Use application/issue dates only after prompt publication or archived snapshots are proven; never reconstruct historical active stock from current status.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Event dates cover 23/23 in principle; 0/23 publication timing verified.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After permission resolution: one two-row SODA projection containing only permit type/status and event dates.
biggest_failure_reason: A present extract may not preserve the historical state or prove when each event was public.

dataset: Adjudication Enforcement Detailed Hearings Data for OBES
economic_mechanism: STR hearing establishment, hearing and violation counts measure enforcement intensity and regulatory friction.
predicted_direction: More hearings/violations per licensed permit should reduce active supply or raise host friction.
why_underused: Parcel-level adjudication workflow is nonstandard administrative exhaust requiring category mapping and vintage controls.
plausible_abnb_materiality: Strong local mechanism in an event-driven STR market; limited consolidated scale.
history: All hearings from Jan. 1 2018; portal created Aug. 17 2022.
publication_schedule_and_lag: Current portal updated periodically; exact event-to-publication lag unverified.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Event dates plus current/open violation and judgment fields that may revise.
access_method: Socrata SODA API view uzyk-jrck and CSV export.
license_or_reuse: Portal marks public access; exact dataset licence/automation terms unresolved
collection_restrictions: No direct request until terms and robots allow; filter agency/case type to STR; exclude address and incident identifiers.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Case backfill before portal creation, rescheduled hearings, changing agency/case codes, duplicated events, revised judgments.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Pre-2022 event rows may have been backfilled; current open violations/judgment are later states.
leakage_mitigation: Start no earlier than portal creation unless historical release evidence exists; use only immutable event dates proven promptly published.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After permission resolution: one two-row SODA projection with agency/type/event dates/counts only.
biggest_failure_reason: Enforcement activity may be policy effort and backfilled workflow data rather than timely supply removal.

dataset: Active licenses for Short-Term Residential Occupancy
provider: City of San Diego Office of the City Treasurer
economic_mechanism: Active STRO licence counts by tier and planning area measure legal host capacity under a capped/licensed regime.
predicted_direction: More active licences should increase supply capacity; expiry clustering may foreshadow attrition.
potential_abnb_target: active supply; nights booked; U.S. geographic mix
why_underused: Tier caps, Mission Beach carve-out and licence expirations create municipal supply signals not in broad travel datasets.
plausible_abnb_materiality: Large coastal leisure/convention market but one city remains a limited ABNB share.
history: Dataset issued Jan. 19 2023; current active file updated Sep. 1 2026.
publication_schedule_and_lag: Portal updates current active file; exact frequency blank in indexed metadata.
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Overwritten active-only CSV; expiration date present; issue date absent.
access_method: Official CSV download offered on data portal; MapServer also available.
license_or_reuse: City terms; FAQ says no restrictions on usage/redistribution
collection_restrictions: Robots unresolved; source includes names, phones, addresses and tax IDs that must never be collected or retained; project only tier/planning area/expiration.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Active-only survivorship, renewal/expiry cycles, tier lotteries, policy caps, blank update-frequency metadata.
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Today's active list cannot reconstruct historical active licences; expiration date is not issue date.
leakage_mitigation: Prospective timestamped snapshots only; aggregate on ingest and discard row-level payload; never backfill history.
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: 0/23 historical events; prospective only after permission.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: After robots resolution: one CSV or MapServer query returning only tier, planning area and expiration for at most two records.
biggest_failure_reason: The active-only snapshot has no defensible historical reconstruction and contains avoidable personal data fields.

dataset: U.S. Automatic Identification System historical vessel positions
provider: MarineCadastre.gov partnership of BOEM NOAA and USCG
economic_mechanism: Passenger-vessel and ferry movements into island/coastal ports can proxy realized access and disruptions; cruise vessels must be separated because they may substitute for lodging
predicted_direction: Positive for ferries/recreational arrivals; ambiguous or negative for cruise
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; geographic mix; travel disruption
why_underused: Raw AIS is technically heavy, vessel classification is imperfect and separating complementary ferries from substitute cruises requires fixed port geofences and vessel classes
plausible_abnb_materiality: Potentially scalable across many island/coastal destinations
unit_of_observation: Timestamped AIS vessel position/transit with MMSI and vessel-type attributes
frequency: Raw messages high frequency; bulk publication commonly annual
history: AccessAIS page currently exposes 2020-2025 range; historical bulk downloads available separately
publication_schedule_and_lag: Bulk publication lag and earliest exact year not established from official evidence retrieved
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: 2020 start shown in active subset tool; older bulk history unresolved
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Annual/bulk products may be regenerated; subset ordering service status can change
access_method: Official bulk downloads; AccessAIS subset service currently unavailable
credential_requirement: AccessAIS subset orders request an email; bulk downloads appear no-key
license_or_reuse: Federal public data; NOAA/BOEM/USCG attribution; exact AIS reuse notice to verify
collection_restrictions: Do not submit email/order or automate until service and robots/terms evidence are clear; no vessel owner or person data retained
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: AIS gaps/spoofing; vessel-type miscoding; coastal receiver coverage; changing carriage mandates; port/geofence changes; cruise substitution
point_in_time_leakage_risk: Using a current reprocessed annual file as historical vintage or inferring passenger counts from positions
historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: Potential raw observation coverage for most/all 23 events but 0/23 strict availability verified; subset service unavailable
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One bulk index and one tiny pre-aggregated port-day if service returns
biggest_failure_reason: Operational service is unavailable and annual publication timing is likely too late for same-quarter forecasting
analyst_notes: Preserve as moonshot infrastructure; not ready for historical pilot

provider: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation / 311
economic_mechanism: Weekend-night noise and illegal-hotel complaints per fixed tourism district may proxy visitor density or regulatory/enforcement stress relative to residential control districts
predicted_direction: Ambiguous: positive for visitor stress but negative for regulatory friction
potential_abnb_target: Nights booked; active supply; geographic mix
why_underused: Complaint microdata are public and frequent, but extracting a fixed no-PII aggregate and controlling reporting-channel changes is operationally nonstandard
plausible_abnb_materiality: One globally material destination but city-level outcomes are unavailable in ABNB disclosures
unit_of_observation: Service request with created date, problem/detail, agency and aggregate geography
granularity: Service-request event; aggregate only to council district/borough
publication_schedule_and_lag: Automatically updated daily; current values for many fields change over time
earliest_verifiable_public_availability: 2011-10-18 date made public for the longstanding dataset
revision_or_snapshot_policy: Mutable rows; 2025 field-label additions and dataset split; Socrata changelog/restore points visible but programmatic vintage guarantees not established
access_method: Socrata SODA/OData with server-side aggregation only; portal restore points are not yet verified as complete historical snapshots.
license_or_reuse: NYC Open Data terms allow public dataset use with source/version/modification identification
collection_restrictions: Query only aggregate counts; never select or retain addresses, BBL, coordinates, free text, or complainant data; robots evidence required.
sensor_methodology_survivorship_risks: Complaint-channel changes; enforcement campaigns; category renames; reporting propensity; duplicate complaints; COVID regime; mutable closure/status fields.

historical_guidance_cutoff_coverage: History spans 23/23 events, but 0/23 are strict-eligible until complete restore-point coverage or contemporaneous aggregates are proven.
smallest_lawful_validation_sample: One metadata response plus one server-side aggregate count with no location microdata; gate denied, so zero requests.
biggest_failure_reason: Complaints measure reporting and enforcement behavior, not tourist presence, and vintage reconstruction is unresolved.

dataset: Pedestrian Counting System counts per hour
provider: City of Melbourne Open Data Team
